stem: Who is the Executive Head of State in India?
expl: According to Article 53(1), the executive power of the Union shall be vested in the President, and shall be exercised in accordance with the Constitution, either directly or through officers subordinate to the President. Thus, the President is the Executive Head of the Indian Union.

stem: The President:

options.label: a
options.text: is not a part of the Parliament

options.label: b
options.text: is a part of the Parliament

options.label: c
options.text: is a part of the Parliament and sits in the Parliament

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The President of India, together with the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, constitutes Parliament. Thus, the President is an integral part of Parliament. It is noteworthy that in a parliamentary system, the executive is responsible to the legislature for its policies and actions. Parliamentary government is also called “Cabinet Government” or “Responsible Government” or the “Westminster model of government.”

expl: The supreme command of the Indian Armed Forces is vested in the President of India. The responsibility for national defence lies with the Council of Ministers, and it is carried out through the Ministry of Defence.

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: According to the Indian Constitution, there shall be a President of India (Article 52). The executive power of the Union shall be vested in the President, and shall be exercised in accordance with the Constitution, either directly or through officers subordinate to the President [Article 53(1)].

stem: The Indian President is eligible for re-election for how many times?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Article 57 of the Indian Constitution deals with eligibility for re-election to the office of President. According to it, a person who holds or has held office as President shall, subject to the other provisions of the Constitution, be eligible for re-election to that office. Thus, the President of India can be re-elected any number of times.

stem: Electoral College for the election of the President of India consists of all -

options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: Article 54 of the Constitution provides for the members of the President’s Electoral College, which includes the following members— (1) Elected members of both Houses of Parliament (2) Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States (3) Elected members of the Legislative Assembliesof Delhi and Puducherry (inserted by the Constitution (Seventieth Amendment) Act, 1992). Members of the State Legislative Councils are not included in this Electoral College. note : Elected members of the Legislative Assembly of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir have not yet been included in the President’s Electoral College.

stem: If there is any dispute regarding the Presidential election, it can be referred to –
expl: If there is any dispute regarding the election of the President of India, then according to Article 71(1), it shall be referred to the Supreme Court of India, and the decision given by the Supreme Court shall be final.

stem: Which one of the following is electoral college for the President but not forum for his impeachment?
expl: According to Article 61 of the Constitution of India, impeachment of the President is a quasi-judicial process conducted in Parliament. The State Legislative Assemblies do not participate in it, whereas under Article 54(b), the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies are part of the President’s Electoral College. It should be noted that State Legislative Councils are not part of the President’s Electoral College.

stem: If the position of President and vice-President are vacant, who officiates as the President of India?
expl: According to Article 65, if the office of the President becomes vacant due to death, resignation, or removal, the Vice-President shall discharge the functions of the President. If, for any reason, the Vice-President is also not available, then the Chief Justice of India, or, in his absence, the senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court who is available at that time, shall perform the functions of the President, as provided under the President (Discharge of Functions) Act, 1969.

stem: The President of India can be removed from his post by –
expl: According to Article 56, clause (1), sub-clause (b), for violation of the Constitution, the President can be removed through impeachment conducted by Parliament in the manner provided in Article 61 (Article 61—Procedure for impeachment of the President)

stem: The President of India does not have the right to –

options.label: b
options.text: Remove a judge of Supreme Court

expl: According to Article 124, clause (4) of the Constitution of India, a Judge of the Supreme Court shall not be removed from his office except by an order of the President passed after an address by each House of Parliament, supported by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting, in the same session, and presented to the President for such removal on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity. Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.

stem: What is the sequence number of Ms. Pratibha Patil as the President of the Republic of India?
expl: On 19 July 2007, the 13th Presidential election of the Indian Republic was held. On 25 July 2007, Mrs. Pratibha Devi Singh Patil took oath as the 12th President of the country in terms of persons; however, in terms of tenure order, her rank was 14th. Pratibha Patil defeated Bhairon Singh Shekhawat, the candidate of the National Democratic Alliance. She was the first woman President of India. At present, Droupadi Murmu is the President of India.

stem: The Prime Minister of India is the head of-

options.label: c
options.text: Both the state and central government

expl: According to Article 74(1) of the Constitution of India, there shall be a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President, with the Prime Minister as its head, and the President shall act in accordance with such advice while exercising functions. Thus, the Prime Minister is the practical head of the Central Government. In reality, the Prime Minister is the leader of the party or coalition that has a majority in the Lok Sabha.

stem: Prime Minister of India is generally-
expl: As per the Constitution, the Prime Minister may be a member of either House of Parliament. Generally, however, the Prime Minister is a member of the Lok Sabha, because the Lok Sabha is directly elected by the people and represents the democratically elected government. Still, there is no restriction on a Prime Minister being from the Rajya Sabha, though it is considered more democratic if the Prime Minister is a member of the Lok Sabha.

stem:
Consider the following statements about Central Government:
1. Ministries and Departments are formed by the Prime Minister with consultation of the Cabinet Secretary.
2. Every Minister is allocated Ministry by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister. Out of these:
expl: Under Article 77(3), the President makes rules for the more convenient transaction of the business of the Government of India and for the allocation of that business among ministers. Accordingly, the Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961 were made, which list the ministries/ departments and their subjects. New ministries/departments are created or reorganised by amending these rules through presidential amendments. As per these rules, the President allocates portfolios among ministers on the advice of the Prime Minister. Therefore, statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.

stem: In Indian Polity, the executive is subordinate to the-
expl: India has adopted the parliamentary system of government. In this system, the executive works under the control of the legislature because the political executive is generally formed from among the members of the legislature, and the executive (Council of Ministers) is collectively responsible to the legislature (Lok Sabha).

stem: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts restricted the size of the Council of Ministers to 15 percent of the total members of the lok Sabha?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: By the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003, clause (1- A) was added to Article 75 of the Constitution, providing that the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Union Council of Ministers shall not exceed 15% of the total membership of the Lok Sabha. Therefore, option (c) is the correct answer.
